A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NGA research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including material relocated between versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original MCES, graph similarity, and retrieval experiments on AIDS, MOLHIV, and MCF-7, plus ablations and empirical analyses in Appendices F–G.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds Gurobi comparisons, a positive-temperature ablation, exact-optimum frequencies, and general QAP evaluations.

M1.justification: Appendix G.5 introduces a limited QAP adaptation that omits ACG construction and applies the existing NGA module directly. The main MCES method retains its GNN initialization, product temperature parameterization, Sinkhorn updates, objective, and decoding procedures.

E1.justification: v2 extends evaluation beyond molecular MCES, similarity, and retrieval to general quadratic assignment using synthetic location-and-facility-flow problems and QAPLIB instances. This adds a distinct optimization task and data domain; the original molecular coverage remains.

E2.justification: Gurobi joins the MCES comparison in Table 1. New QAP comparisons evaluate SM and NeuOpt in Table 7, and PATH, GLAG, and FAQ in Table 8. These substantially expand the evaluated comparator set; the original comparison methods remain.

E3.justification: The new synthetic QAP protocol specifies 20/50/100-node problems, up to 5,120 training instances, 256 test instances, and total assignment cost. v2 also evaluates 16 QAPLIB cases and adds exact-optimum frequency and a positive-temperature control. Existing MCES splits, training budgets, and time limits are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds NGA-Positive, using a sigmoid to restrict temperature to positive values, to test the exploration rationale. Appendix G.1 adds analysis of how frequently NGA finds an exact optimum. Existing component ablations, sensitivity plots, and case studies remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the mean and ±1 standard-deviation displays in Figures 11–12. No new seed counts, repeated-run disclosures, confidence intervals, or statistical testing procedures appear; the added tables report point estimates.

E6.justification: New results include Gurobi MCES accuracies of 74.52/78.67/80.76 on AIDS/MOLHIV/MCF-7, NGA-Positive scores, and exact-optimum rates of 49%/56%/61% on AIDS/MCF-7/MOLHIV. Tables 7–8 add QAP results: NGA beats NeuOpt on QAP50/100 but trails it on QAP20. Original main scores are retained, with GLSearch's malformed 41..12 entry corrected to 41.12.

T1.justification: Appendix C.3 replaces the dense O(mkN^4) NGA complexity estimate with O(mk(M+N^2)), using M ACG edges and molecular sparsity, and revises corresponding baseline bounds. Section 3's displayed relaxation drops the entropy term. The proposed objective and substantive proofs in Appendices B, D, and E remain unchanged.

C1.justification: v2 explicitly claims the first ACG-based MCES formulation and the first theoretical analysis of dynamic, parameterized temperatures in NGA. v1's priority claim focused on the first neural-style MCES solver. The central accuracy, scalability, and application claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the positive-temperature ablation as supporting the importance of negative temperatures, and the QAP results as evidence of broader applicability. Section 5 removes the explicit assertion that traditional GA lacks exploration. The labeled-versus-unlabeled graph limitation is unchanged and relocated to Appendix H.

D1.justification: Appendix G.5 adds QAP generation instructions, including uniform coordinates and flows, symmetrization, zero diagonals, and 70% flow zeroing, alongside training/test counts. Appendix F documents the sigmoid restriction. Original MCES implementation and hardware details remain, while v1's explicit GA pseudocode is removed.

R1.justification: Six cited works are added for QAPLIB, SM, NeuOpt, GLAG, FAQ, and PATH. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion de-emphasize NGA's direct derivation from classical GA in favor of annealing-inspired parameterized optimization and stronger priority claims. The existing related-work survey and earlier references are retained.

P1.justification: v2 adds introductory paragraph labels and makes targeted rewrites to the abstract, motivation, preliminaries, and conclusion. GA background is condensed into Appendix A, Appendix G is expanded and renumbered, and limitations move to Appendix H. The overall narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 6–8 and expands Tables 1 and 5 with new rows. Existing figures, including Figures 3, 4, 7, and 9, are relocated, and Figure 1's caption is revised. All thirteen figures retain their graphical content; there is no broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 supplements v1's near-optimal average accuracies with exact-optimum frequencies and a positive-temperature control, clarifying solution quality and providing a more direct test of the temperature mechanism. Gurobi and QAP comparisons broaden validation. These gains are limited by brief settings for the new comparisons and reduced explicit GA background and pseudocode; the core results and proofs remain unchanged.
